reasons: Claimed status is compliant and the redline is identical to the original text with no comment, which is the expected output for a compliant finding.

The cited clauses support the fallback: Section 5(a) imposes a monthly minimum, but Section 13 caps the term at one year with successive one-year renewals and a 30-day non-renewal right, and Section 14 lets Client terminate at will with the minimum ceasing at the end of the month following notice.

No shortfall penalty, make-whole, or acceleration of unused minimums appears in the cited text, so the exit operates prospectively rather than as a penalty — consistent with the fallback's true-up requirement and well clear of the multi-year take-or-pay walk-away.

The rationale correctly notes it sits at the fallback rather than preferred, and correctly declines to flag the programmer-availability commitment, which runs in our favour, and defers the billing-transparency carve-out in Section 6 to the audit/disputes rule (no double-flagging).
Blank dollar figures are appropriately noted as a drafting point rather than escalated as a deviation under this presence rule.
